title: The Last Message
incident: A classified intercept decrypt ('Operation Cerberus') was leaked to an encrypted paste site at 4:12 PM. The document was stored on an air-gapped terminal. Five senior intelligence analysts had legitimate clearance, and all five were seated in the SCIF during the incident.
centralQuestions: How did an air-gapped decrypt reach the public internet?
Did the analyst whose smartcard signed the terminal session physically execute the export command?
What role did the optical air-gap bridge (acoustic or LED modulation) play?

timeline.event: Operation Cerberus decrypted on air-gapped Terminal 7.
Analyst Samuel Ward inserts PIV smartcard into Terminal 7.
Terminal 7 status LED blinks rapidly for 180 seconds.
Encrypted text posted to Pastebin from an external IP address in Stockholm.
SCIF lockdown initiated; all five analysts detained.

suspects.name: Samuel Ward
suspects.motive: Ideological whistleblower; sympathetic to public privacy advocacy.
suspects.statement: He says he was analyzing the decrypt header and left his smartcard inserted while fetching water from the SCIF cooler.
relevant_evidence: His smartcard authenticated the terminal session at 3:45 PM.
supporting_evidence: SCIF camera shows him at the water cooler from 4:00 PM to 4:04 PM.
suspicious_evidence: His card was active during the 4:02 PM LED anomaly.
suspects.uncertainty: Water cooler footage confirms he was not touching the keyboard at 4:02 PM.
open_questions: Who touched Terminal 7 while Samuel was at the cooler?

suspects.name: Kira Vance
suspects.motive: Blackmailed by overseas intelligence over family assets.
suspects.statement: She says she was debugging assembly code at Terminal 5 with headphones on.
relevant_evidence: Possesses deep knowledge of optical and acoustic air-gap exfiltration.
Smartphone found in personal locker had a light sensor app installed.
supporting_evidence: Terminal 5 debugger logs show continuous compilation.
suspicious_evidence: A custom firmware binary was compiled on her workstation at 3:30 PM.
suspects.uncertainty: Compiling firmware is her daily professional duty.
open_questions: Could she exfiltrate data via LED light modulation?

suspects.name: David O'Connor
suspects.motive: Disputed promotion; leaked compliance flaws in the past.
suspects.statement: He says he was walking around the SCIF conducting random clean-desk audits.
relevant_evidence: Had clipboard with reflective metallic surface.
suspicious_evidence: Stood behind Samuel's terminal while Samuel was at the water cooler.
suspects.uncertainty: Walking around terminals is his explicit job duty.
open_questions: Did he initiate a macro on Samuel's keyboard?

witnesses.name: SCIF Monitor Guard
witnesses.statement: No digital media (USB, phones, or wireless transmitters) were brought into the SCIF.
witnesses.limitations: Does not detect optical light frequencies through viewing glass.

evidence.title: Terminal 7 Keyboard Event Trace
evidence.description: Keystrokes 'Ctrl+Shift+F12' (custom macro hotkey) executed at 4:01:45 PM while Ward was at the water cooler.
evidence.establishes: Someone touched Ward's keyboard while Ward was getting water.

evidence.title: LED Optical Modulation Log
evidence.description: High-speed camera records Terminal 7 hard-drive activity LED pulsing in Morse/Manchester encoded binary at 4:02 PM toward the exterior window glass.
evidence.establishes: Data was transmitted optically across the physical air gap via LED flashes.
evidence.does_not_establish: Who received the optical pulses outside the building.

evidence.title: Clipboard Angle Reflection
evidence.description: Security video shows O'Connor angling his metallic clipboard to reflect the Terminal 7 LED toward the window sensor across the street.
evidence.establishes: O'Connor physically facilitated the optical light path redirect.
evidence.does_not_establish: Whether he wrote the optical software.

evidence.title: VPN Bastion Session Anomaly
evidence.description: An encrypted SSH session originated from a jump-host inside the data center at 2:03 AM while badge records showed the engineer at home.
evidence.establishes: The privileged shell was triggered remotely via an internal proxy.
evidence.does_not_establish: Physical location of the operator behind the jump-host.

evidence.title: Clipboard Synchronization Dump
evidence.description: Shared virtual desktop clipboard cache preserved the plaintext draft of the leaked memo with timestamps matching the contractor workstation.
evidence.establishes: The memo was copied into local system clipboard buffer.
evidence.does_not_establish: Whether automated spyware or human operator triggered the copy.

redHerrings: Samuel Ward's smartcard was active, making him the obvious technical culprit, but video proves he was standing at the water cooler during the keypress.
Kira Vance compiled firmware, but her binary was an official anti-rootkit patch verified by agency checksums.

hiddenSolution.explanation: David O'Connor waited until Samuel Ward stepped away to the water cooler, struck the pre-loaded macro hotkey on Terminal 7 at 4:01 PM, and used his polished metallic clipboard as a mirror to bounce the pulsing optical LED signals through the SCIF window to an operative waiting with a telephoto receiver across the street in a parked van.
uncertainties: Identity of the foreign handler in the van across the street
hiddenSolution.alternativeExplanation: Kira Vance deployed an autonomous background daemon that triggered the LED pulse without human intervention.

missingEvidence: Forensic search of the parked surveillance van across the street
rules: A smartcard login does not establish who pressed the keys minutes later.
Air-gapped systems can be exfiltrated via non-radio optical or acoustic side-channels.
